correctness.rationale: The classical 3-term Sylvester/Curtiss bound gives beta=41/42 uniquely at (2,3,7). For any other triple prefix and total >beta, the strict rational inequalities x_(j+1)<(4-j)/(beta-s_j) bound each next denominator without a search cutoff. These yield 21 possible triples including one special prefix, 20 other triples in seven listed groups. Each has maximal under-1 fourth denominator max(z,floor[1/(1-s)]+1); rational comparisons give unique maximum 599/600 at (2,3,8,25). Independent exact-fraction derivation recovered these 21 prefixes and unique maximum. For theta>629/630 the special greedy last denominator <=45 and its value >=629/630>599/600, proving uniqueness; on the adjacent interval strict target greed forces 46 and loses. Universal theta statement follows from finite *exhaustive algebraic bounds*, not bounded empirical scan.

value.rationale: This supplies a sharp boundary of greedy optimality on an open real interval for exactly four Egyptian reciprocals, together with a natural second-best extremum 599/600. It answers a motivated fixed-length underapproximation stability question with fully exhaustive rational bounds and a uniquely identified obstruction, not an arbitrary four-tuple computation.

final_claim: For every real theta in (629/630,1], the unique best strict four-term Egyptian underapproximation is (2,3,7,floor[1/(theta-41/42)]+1). The endpoint is sharp: for theta in (599/600,629/630], (2,3,8,25) strictly beats the greedy (2,3,7,46).
limitations: Exactly four nondecreasing positive integer denominators with first >=2; strict underapproximation; no full phase diagram.
Comparisons use exact rational bounds, and independent enumeration is only confirmatory of the bounded case list.
